patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff did not apply to the staged vulnerable checkout because its ChangeLog context diverged, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative n132/arvo:42510080-fix image instrumented with the same frozen assertions. In that real fixed build the remainder-copy path in libelf/gelf_xlate.c initializes the full 28-byte MOVE buffer before elf_compress_gnu() reaches memcmp.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: Source. libelf first materializes the attacker-controlled section-count and section-table offset fields from the big-endian ELF header into host-endian local state.

Root cause. The shared xlate macro iterates in units of the native `Elf64_Move` size, but this witness was admitted as a single 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` record. For the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch reached here, `len` is 28 and `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32 on the saved x86_64 build, so the loop count is zero and the vulnerable converter returns without writing any bytes to the freshly allocated destination buffer.

MSAN sink. This GNU-header check reaches `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)`, which reads the first four bytes of the translated section-5 buffer after `convert_data()` published a 28-byte heap allocation that `Elf64_cvt_Move` left untouched.

nodes.state: After Elf64_cvt_Move returns, convert_data() publishes the same 28-byte buffer with zero initialized bytes as the first Elf_Data payload returned by elf_getdata().

edges.evidence: The traces record move_conversion_tail.dest_buf_ptr == published_move_data.published_buf_ptr for both vulnerable and fixed executions.
The traces record published_move_data.published_buf_ptr == gnu_memcmp_probe.sink_buf_ptr for both vulnerable and fixed executions.

verification_limitations: The official patch.diff did not apply to the staged checkout. Fixed-side evidence therefore comes from the authoritative n132/arvo:42510080-fix image rather than an incremental patch application on the staged vulnerable tree.

The ARVO compile wrapper dirtied the checkout with build-only files such as zlib/, so the final vulnerable and fixed runtime captures were taken directly from /bin/arvo run inside the instrumented containers after the corresponding builds completed.
